newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech govt sets 5-yr flood bonds at 12.5pct 1st yr.
newsitem.headline: Czech govt sets 5-yr flood bonds at 12.5pct 1st yr.

text.p: The Czech government has set a public issue of one billion crowns in five-year flood relief bonds with a fixed rate of 12.5 percent for the first year, the finance ministry said on Thursday.
The final four years of maturity would have an interest rate equal to the average inflation rate for the previous 12 months plus 250 basis points.
The primary retail sale through major Czech banks will be conducted from August 1-15 without change to the interest rate offered, and from August 16-29 with a prorated interest rate.
The bonds, with an issue date of August 1, have withholding tax of 25 percent of the coupon paid, the standard Czech securities rate.
Nominal value of the bonds will be 1,000 and 10,000 crowns, and the bonds will be in bearer form. The coupon is to be paid once yearly.

The Czech government has approved up to five billion crowns in domestic bond issues to help pay for relief efforts in the eastern part of the country which has been devastated by floods brought on by torrential rains last week.
Further details on other possible issues have not been released.
